examples.problem:
A particle $P$ is traveling along the $x$-axis with displacement $s(t)$ from a fixed origin $O$ given by

$$
s(t) = t^3-3t^2+12t,\quad t\geq 0.
$$

Find the time at which the acceleration is zero, and find the value of the velocity at this moment.
examples.worked_solution:
First, we calculate $v(t)$ by differentiating $s(t)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}+12t) \\  & =3{t}^{2}-6t+12\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we differentiate $v(t)$ to find $a(t)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}-6t+12) \\  & =6t-6\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we put $a=0$ to find the time when the acceleration is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}0 & =6t-6 \\ 6t & =6 \\ t & =1\end{aligned}
$$

So the acceleration is zero when $t=1$. To find the velocity at this moment, we substitute this back into $v(t)$ to get

$$
v(1) = 3(1)^2 - 6(1)+12 = 9.
$$

feedback.problem:
The displacement $s,$ in meters, relative to a fixed origin $O$ of a particle moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis is given by $s(t)=3t{e}^{-2t},$ where $t>0$ is the time, measured in seconds. Find the time intervals in which the particle is moving in the direction of decreasing $x.$

$t\in (${{field-1}},

{{field-2}}$)$
feedback.worked_solution:
If the particle moves in the direction of decreasing $x,$ then its velocity is negative. 

First, we calculate the velocity function by differentiating the position function:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3t{e}^{-2t}) \\  & =3{e}^{-2t}+3t(-2){e}^{-2t} \\  & =(3-6t){e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate time intervals in which the particle is moving in the direction of decreasing $x$, we solve $v(t)<0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & <0 \\ (3-6t){e}^{-2t} & <0 \\ 3-6t & <0 \\ -6t & <-3 \\ t & >\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the time interval in which the particle is moving to the direction of decreasing $x$ is 

$$
t\in (\frac{1}{2},\infty ).
$$
